- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment remains bullish.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period rallies (last 5–7 days of forecast horizon); apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 2–3% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; adjust by adding 0.3–0.8% to forecast if sentiment shifts sharply mid-horizon.
